sample_unit: published dermatomyositis cases with clinical images

links.outcome: Agreement between multimodal LLM and expert rheumatologists on CDASI scoring (standalone, no human-with-AI comparison)
links.effect: Global activity ICC 0.71 (95% CI 0.45-0.86); damage ICC 0.41 (95% CI 0.25-0.67); hand global ICC 0.95. Standalone agreement only; no with/without AI user comparison.
links.quote: Global CDASI activity showed good agreement with expert raters (ICC 0.71, 95% CI 0.45-0.86), whereas damage reliability was lower (ICC 0.41, 95% CI 0.25-0.67).

unlisted_practices: Using a multimodal LLM to automate CDASI scoring from clinical images to reduce clinician scoring time (42 s vs 8.4 min per case)

screen.reason: The study evaluates the accuracy and inter-rater agreement of Claude 3.5 Sonnet compared to expert rheumatologists on CDASI scoring using published clinical images. It does not test a specific deployment safeguard or practice.
